heroData.title: Hire in Saudi Arabia Without a Local Entity
heroData.subtitle: Saudization-Compliant Workforce Solutions
heroData.description: Legally employ Saudi nationals and expatriates across the Kingdom without establishing a local entity. Our EOR handles GOSI registration, Iqama sponsorship, Nitaqat compliance, and full payroll through the Wage Protection System (WPS).
heroData.bestFor: International firms entering the Saudi market under Vision 2030 mega-projects.

sections.title: Iqama & Work Permit Process
sections.subtitle: 4-8 Weeks Timeline
sections.description: Comprehensive visa sponsorship oversight for skilled and unskilled labor in KSA.

steps.title: MHRSD Work Visa Application
steps.description: Submit the work visa request through the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) Qiwa portal.

steps.title: MOFA Visa Block Issuance
steps.description: Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues the visa block (authorization number) for the Saudi Embassy in the worker's home country.

steps.title: Medical Examination
steps.description: Mandatory medical fitness test at an approved GAMCA center in the home country before travel.

steps.title: Iqama Issuance
steps.description: Upon arrival, register biometrics and obtain the Iqama (residency permit) via Absher within 90 days of entry.

steps.title: GOSI Registration
steps.description: Enroll the employee in the General Organization for Social Insurance within 15 days of employment start.

steps.title: Muqeem Profile Setup
steps.description: Create the employee's digital profile on the Muqeem portal for ongoing visa and exit/re-entry management.

sections.title: Saudization (Nitaqat) Compliance
sections.subtitle: Mandatory Quota System
sections.description: Critical workforce nationalization requirements that directly affect EOR operations.

items.title: Nitaqat Color Bands
items.text: Companies are classified into Platinum, Green (Low/Mid/High), Yellow, and Red bands based on Saudization percentage. Red-band companies face work permit bans and cannot renew Iqamas.

items.title: 2025 Sector Quotas
items.text: Retail requires 70% Saudi employees. IT/Telecom requires 25%. Construction requires 10%. Healthcare administration requires 30%. Hospitality targets 40%.

items.title: Non-Compliance Penalties
items.text: Failure to meet Nitaqat targets results in SAR 500-800/month per missing Saudi employee, plus restrictions on issuing new work permits.

items.title: EOR Advantage
items.text: Using an EOR with a Green/Platinum Nitaqat rating allows hiring expatriates without quota restrictions on the client's own entity.

sections.title: Mandatory Employee Benefits
sections.subtitle: Saudi Labor Law Entitlements
sections.description: Statutory benefits required for all employees under Saudi employment law.

items.title: Annual Leave
items.text: 21 days for the first 5 years of service, increasing to 30 days thereafter. Employees can carry over up to half their entitlement.

items.title: End of Service Gratuity
items.text: Half month's wage per year for the first 5 years, and one full month per year thereafter. Payable upon contract termination.

items.title: Health Insurance (CCHI)
items.text: Mandatory medical insurance through CCHI-accredited providers for all employees and their dependents. Minimum coverage set by the Council of Cooperative Health Insurance.

items.title: Housing Allowance
items.text: While not legally mandatory, market practice is 25% of basic salary. Most candidates expect it as part of the total compensation package.

sections.title: Monthly Payroll Cycle
sections.subtitle: WPS & GOSI Workflow
sections.description: Standard process for salary disbursement and statutory filings in KSA.

steps.title: Data Consolidation
steps.description: Gather basic salary, housing allowance (25%), transport allowance, and variable commissions for all staff.

steps.title: GOSI Calculation
steps.description: Calculate employer and employee contributions: 12% employer + 10% employee for Saudis; 2% employer for expatriates (OHRP only).

steps.title: WPS File Generation
steps.description: Generate the Wage Protection System file for submission through Mudad platform to MHRSD.

steps.title: Bank Transfer
steps.description: Disburse salaries via SAMA-approved banks. Wages must be paid by the 7th of the following month.

steps.title: Payslip Distribution
steps.description: Issue detailed Arabic/English payslips showing gross, deductions, GOSI splits, and net amounts.

sections.title: GOSI Contribution Rates 2025-2026
sections.subtitle: New Social Insurance Law
sections.description: Updated contribution rates under the new Social Insurance Law effective July 2024.

items.title: Saudi Nationals (Annuities)
items.text: Employer pays 12% and employee pays 10% of monthly contributory wage for the Annuities branch (pension). Total: 22%. Starting July 2025, rates increase by 0.5% annually for new subscribers.

items.title: Expatriates (OHRP)
items.text: Employer pays 2% of monthly wage for Occupational Hazards and Risk Protection. No employee contribution required for non-Saudis.

items.title: SANED (Unemployment Insurance)
items.text: 1.5% employer + 1% employee for Saudi nationals. Provides up to 60% of average salary for 3 months if involuntarily terminated.

items.title: Contribution Ceiling
items.text: Maximum contributory wage is SAR 45,000/month. Earnings above this cap are not subject to GOSI deductions.

sections.title: Mudad & WPS Compliance
sections.subtitle: Wage Protection Enforcement
sections.description: Critical rules for maintaining compliant salary disbursement in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Mudad Platform
items.text: All private sector employers must register on Mudad and submit monthly salary data. Non-compliance leads to work permit restrictions within 60 days.

items.title: Payment Deadline
items.text: Salaries must be paid within 7 days of the due date. Delays beyond this trigger automatic alerts to MHRSD and potential labor system blocks.

items.title: No Personal Income Tax
items.text: Saudi Arabia does not levy personal income tax on employees. Payroll deductions are limited to GOSI and any voluntary deductions.

items.title: Multi-Currency
items.text: SAR is pegged to USD at 3.75. For international staff, consider dual-currency payroll to reduce FX exposure on home remittances.

sections.title: Calculation Logic & Rules
sections.subtitle: Basis for Computation
sections.description: Key factors influencing salary calculations in KSA.

items.title: No Income Tax
items.text: There is NO personal income tax in Saudi Arabia. Gross salary is only subject to GOSI deduction (for Saudi nationals).

items.title: GOSI Base (Nationals)
items.text: Deduction is 22.5% of [Basic Salary + Housing]. Capped at SAR 45,000/month. 12.25% paid by Employer, 10.25% by Employee (approx. 2025 rates).

items.title: Expats Cost
items.text: Expats pay 0% GOSI. Employer pays 2% (Occupational Hazards) capped at SAR 45,000 earnings. Total cost is Gross + 2% + Health Insurance.

items.title: End of Service
items.text: Accrual must be factored for employer cost: 0.5 salary/year for first 5 years, 1 salary/year thereafter.

heroData.title: Saudi Arabia Company Formation
heroData.subtitle: MISA Licensed Entity Setup
heroData.description: Establish your legal presence in the Kingdom with 100% foreign ownership. From MISA investment license and CR registration to ZATCA tax enrollment & commercial bank account opening, we manage the entire incorporation lifecycle.
heroData.bestFor: Global enterprises entering the Saudi market under Vision 2030 investment reforms.

sections.title: Company Formation Roadmap
sections.subtitle: 4-12 Weeks Timeline
sections.description: Standard procedure for establishing a legal entity in Saudi Arabia.

steps.title: MISA Investment License
steps.description: Apply for the Ministry of Investment license via the MISA portal. Required for all foreign investors. Processing: 5-15 business days.

steps.title: Entity Type Selection
steps.description: Choose between LLC (most common, min SAR 500K capital), Branch Office (no separate legal personality), or Joint Stock Company.

steps.title: Articles of Association
steps.description: Draft and notarize the MOA/AOA at the Ministry of Commerce (MoC). Must be in Arabic and signed by all shareholders.

steps.title: Commercial Registration (CR)
steps.description: Obtain the CR number from MoC. This is the company's primary legal identifier for all government dealings.

steps.title: ZATCA Registration
steps.description: Register for VAT (15%) and corporate income tax (20% for foreign-owned entities) with Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority.

steps.title: Bank Account Opening
steps.description: Open a corporate account with SAMA-licensed banks (Al Rajhi, SNB, Riyad Bank). Requires CR, MISA license, and board resolution.

sections.title: Foreign Ownership & MISA Rules
sections.subtitle: 100% Foreign Ownership
sections.description: Understanding Saudi Arabia's liberalized investment framework.

items.title: 100% Foreign Ownership
items.text: Saudi Arabia now allows 100% foreign ownership in most sectors without a local partner. The 2024 New Companies Law further simplified entity structures.

items.title: Restricted Activities
items.text: Certain sectors remain restricted: oil exploration, military equipment, and some professional services. Always verify the MISA Negative List before applying.

items.title: Minimum Capital
items.text: LLC minimum capital is SAR 500,000 for most activities. Regional HQ companies benefit from reduced requirements under the RHQ program.

items.title: Regional HQ Program
items.text: Companies establishing their regional headquarters in Riyadh by 2024 receive preferential MISA processing, tax incentives, and priority government contract access.

sections.title: Incorporation Costs & Fees
sections.subtitle: 2025 Fee Schedule
sections.description: Typical government and professional fees for Saudi company setup.

items.label: MISA License Fee
items.description: SAR 2,000 application year + SAR 60,000 subscription for first year (reduced to SAR 2,000 for SMEs/RHQ).

items.label: Commercial Registration
items.description: Main CR registration (5 years). Branch CRs cost SAR 100.

items.label: Chamber of Commerce
items.description: Annual membership fee based on company grade and capital.

items.label: National Address
items.description: Annual registration with Saudi Post cost.

items.label: Professional Fees
items.description: Legal, notary, and agency fees for full setup.

sections.subtitle: Vision 2030 Impact
sections.description: Key hiring trends driven by Saudi Arabia's economic transformation.

items.title: Mega-Project Demand
items.text: NEOM, The Red Sea, Qiddiya, and ROSHN are creating 100,000+ jobs across construction, hospitality, tech, and entertainment. Specialized recruitment firms are essential.

items.title: Salary Inflation
items.text: Tech and finance roles in Riyadh have seen 15-25% salary increases YoY due to RHQ mandate driving demand. Offer competitiveness is critical.

items.title: Female Workforce
items.text: Female labor participation has risen from 17% to 36% since 2016. Companies actively recruiting women benefit from Nitaqat bonus points and HRDF subsidies.

items.title: HRDF Training Subsidies
items.text: The Human Resources Development Fund (Hadaf) reimburses up to 50% of Saudi employee salaries for the first 24 months through the Tamheer and Doam programs.

items.title: PDPL (Royal Decree M/19)
items.text: Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law requires explicit consent for processing employee personal data. Penalties of up to SAR 5 million for violations.

items.title: Data Localization
items.text: Sensitive personal data of Saudi citizens must be stored within KSA borders unless explicitly exempted by SDAIA (Saudi Data & AI Authority).

items.title: Arabic Interface

heroData.subtitle: IFRS & Bookkeeping Services

We handle bilingual bookkeeping (Arabic/English), annual financial statement preparation, and coordination with external auditors to ensure full adherence to Saudi IFRS standards.
heroData.bestFor: All registered entities in KSA requiring statutory compliance.

sections.title: Accounting Standards (SOCPA)
sections.subtitle: IFRS Convergence
sections.description: Regulatory framework for financial reporting in the Kingdom.

items.title: IFRS Mandate
items.text: Large entities must follow full IFRS as endorsed by SOCPA. SMEs are permitted to use IFRS for SMEs. Strict adherence is checked during statutory audits.

items.title: Language Requirements
items.text: All official ledgers, journals, and financial statements must be maintained in Arabic. Bilingual reporting is common for international firms, but Arabic is the legal text.

items.title: Record Retention
items.text: Commercial books must be kept for 10 years. Tax and VAT related documents should be retained for up to 15 years to satisfy ZATCA audit requirements.

sections.title: Annual Accounting Cycle
sections.subtitle: From Bookkeeping to Audit
sections.description: Key financial milestones for Saudi companies.

steps.title: Bilingual Bookkeeping
steps.description: Daily recording of transactions in a ZATCA-compliant ERP. Must support e-invoicing (Fatoora) integration.

steps.title: Quarterly Closing
steps.description: Preparation of interim financial statements, primarily for VAT filing accuracy and management reporting.

steps.title: Year-End Close
steps.description: Finalizing accounts within 3 months of fiscal year-end. reconciling intercompany balances and bank statements.

steps.title: Statutory Audit
steps.description: mandatory audit by a SOCPA-licensed CPA. The audited report is required for renewing the Commercial Registration and MISA license.

steps.title: Qawaem Upload
steps.description: Filing the audited financial statements via the Qawaem portal (Ministry of Commerce) for public record transparency.

sections.title: Saudi Legal System
sections.subtitle: Sharia & Commercial Law
sections.description: Understanding the Kingdom's unique legal framework.

items.title: New Civil Transactions Law
items.text: Enacted in 2023, for the first time codifies contract law, property rights, and tort principles. Provides greater legal certainty for foreign investors.

items.title: Commercial Courts
items.text: Dedicated commercial courts handle business disputes. Cases are heard in Arabic; all documents must be officially translated. Appeals go to the Board of Grievances.

items.title: Arbitration (SCCA)
items.text: The Saudi Center for Commercial Arbitration handles business disputes under UNCITRAL rules. Increasingly preferred by foreign investors for enforcement predictability.

items.title: Labor Disputes
items.text: Employment cases go through MHRSD conciliation first (mandatory 21-day period), then to Labor Courts. Employee-friendly jurisdiction with burden of proof on employer.

sections.title: Contract Execution Process
sections.subtitle: Official Documentation
sections.description: Making contracts legally binding in Saudi Arabia.

steps.title: Arabic Drafting
steps.description: All contracts filed with Saudi courts must be in Arabic. Bilingual versions are common but Arabic text prevails in disputes.

steps.title: Notarization
steps.description: Commercial contracts exceeding SAR 100,000 should be notarized at the Ministry of Justice e-notarization portal.

steps.title: MOFA Attestation
steps.description: Foreign documents require apostille or MOFA attestation for use in Saudi commercial proceedings.

steps.title: Digital Signatures
steps.description: The Absher and Nafath digital signature platforms are legally recognized for electronic contract execution.

sections.title: IP & Trade Secrets
sections.subtitle: SAIP Registration
sections.description: Intellectual property protection in the Kingdom.

items.title: Trademark Registration
items.text: Register with Saudi Authority for Intellectual Property (SAIP). Processing takes 6-12 months. Nice Classification system applied.

items.title: Anti-Commercial Fraud
items.text: Saudi Arabia's Anti-Commercial Fraud Law imposes penalties of up to SAR 1 million and 3 years imprisonment for trademark counterfeiting.

items.title: Trade Secrets
items.text: The 2023 Trade Secrets Law provides explicit protection for confidential business information, trade processes, and proprietary algorithms.

sections.title: Corporate Tax & Zakat
sections.subtitle: Dual Tax Framework
sections.description: Understanding Saudi Arabia's unique approach to business taxation.

items.title: Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
items.text: Foreign-owned entities pay 20% CIT on net adjusted profits. This applies to the foreign investor's share of income from a Saudi-resident company.

items.title: Zakat
items.text: Saudi/GCC-owned companies pay Zakat at 2.5% of the Zakat base (net equity adjusted for certain items) instead of CIT. Zakat applies to the Saudi/GCC ownership portion.

items.title: Mixed Ownership
items.text: JVs with Saudi and foreign shareholders face BOTH: Zakat on the Saudi share and 20% CIT on the foreign share. Requires dual filing with ZATCA.

items.title: WHT Rates
items.text: Withholding tax on payments to non-residents: 5% for dividends, 5% for interest, 15% for royalties and technical fees. Reduced under DTTs.

sections.title: VAT & E-Invoicing Compliance
sections.subtitle: FATOORA System
sections.description: Managing the 15% VAT and mandatory electronic invoicing framework.

steps.title: VAT Registration
steps.description: Mandatory for businesses with annual taxable supplies exceeding SAR 375,000. Voluntary registration threshold: SAR 187,500.

steps.title: E-Invoicing Phase 2 (Integration)
steps.description: FATOORA system requires real-time integration with ZATCA for invoice clearance. All B2B invoices must be cleared before issuance.

steps.title: Quarterly/Monthly VAT Returns
steps.description: File via ZATCA portal. Monthly for revenue > SAR 40M, quarterly for others. Due within 30 days of period end.

steps.title: Record Retention
steps.description: Maintain all tax invoices, credit notes, and accounting records for minimum 6 years as required by ZATCA.

sections.title: Regulatory Framework
sections.subtitle: CMA & GAC Oversight

items.title: Competition Law
items.text: Transactions creating 'Economic Concentration' must be approved by GAC. Fines for non-compliance can reach 10% of annual turnover.

items.title: CMA Regulations
items.text: For listed companies, the Capital Market Authority's M&A Regulations dictate disclosure norms, mandatory offer triggers (50% ownership), and timelines.

items.title: Foreign Investment Law
items.text: Ensure the target activity is not on the Negative List. 100% foreign ownership is widely permitted but some sectors usually require a Saudi partner.

sections.subtitle: NCA & CST Compliance
sections.description: Critical IT compliance requirements for Saudi operations.

items.title: NCA Cybersecurity
items.text: National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA) mandates Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC) for all government and critical infrastructure entities. Private sector compliance increasingly expected.

items.title: Data Localization
items.text: Government data and certain sensitive categories must be hosted within Saudi borders. Cloud providers (AWS ME, Azure, Oracle) now have Riyadh-based data centers.

items.title: CST Licensing
items.text: Communications, Space & Technology Commission (CST) regulates all telecom and ISP services. Special licenses needed for VoIP and satellite comms.

items.title: Cloud-First Policy
items.text: Saudi government's Cloud-First Policy encourages migration to approved cloud platforms. SADAIA provides AI and data analytics frameworks for digital transformation.

items.title: Content Standards
